text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.85% today to $139.65, reversing most of a sharp three-day rally that peaked at $142.28 on November 13th. The stock's pullback comes as crude oil prices have eased slightly—US oil is trading at $89.62 per barrel, down from the levels that likely fueled that earlier jump. With the stock down 4.9% over two weeks despite oil holding in the $89-92 range, today's move appears to be profit-taking after the recent run-up rather than a response to new company-specific news.

The broader context here is mixed signals for energy demand: heating oil prices remain sharply elevated (up 59% year-over-year), which supports refining margins, but rising shipping costs are making retailers cautious on holiday inventory, which could dampen economic activity and energy consumption heading into winter. This kind of uncertainty—pockets of strength offset by signs of consumer caution—may be keeping investors from pushing the stock higher even as oil holds steady.
